headline: French Startup's Magnetic Dyes Cut Fashion's Water Use by 40%
meta_description: EverDye's electrostatic dyeing process uses 40% less water and cuts energy costs by 800%, while delivering vibrant colors that meet industry standards.
summary_short: A French startup has created non-toxic textile dyes that work through magnetism at room temperature, slashing water use, energy, and pollution in fashion manufacturing.
body:
A French startup called EverDye has cracked one of fashion's most stubborn environmental problems: how to dye textiles without consuming vast amounts of water, energy, and toxic chemicals. The company's biowaste and mineral-based pigments use static electricity to bind to fabric—carrying a positive charge that attaches to textiles pre-treated with a negative charge. Because this electrostatic process works at room temperature rather than boiling point, it eliminates the need for heating, cutting production energy costs by 800%. The pigments are non-toxic, require no chemical fixatives, and use approximately 40% less water than conventional dyeing methods while lasting just as long.

Textile dyeing accounts for roughly 20% of global industrial water pollution and represents half of the fashion industry's total emissions. EverDye CEO Philippe Berlan recognized that traditional dyes require high temperatures to adhere to fibers and consume enormous quantities of water and petrochemicals. His team's room-temperature alternative makes economic sense across the industry because when life-cycle costs—energy, water, and additives—are factored in, the approach pencils out even for budget-conscious dyehouses. Better still, factories adopting EverDye's process need minimal hardware changes; employee training is the only real adjustment required.

The approach has already proven itself in practice. Collaborations with brands like AdoreMe have demonstrated that EverDye's pigments achieve vibrant, durable colors meeting the same industry standards for washing and wear as conventional dyes. In summer 2025, the company completed a $17.5 million Series A funding round and plans to scale production to meet broader industry demand. By solving a deeply entrenched problem without compromising quality or requiring massive infrastructure overhauls, EverDye is showing that sustainable fashion innovation can be both environmentally sound and commercially viable.
